subject: general
question: Kharavela was an important ruler of which dynasty?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chedi Dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kharavela was a prominent ruler of the **Chedi Dynasty**, which ruled over Kalinga (modern-day Odisha).
 
• He is known for his military conquests, administrative capabilities, and contributions to art and culture in ancient India.
 
• The **Hathigumpha Inscription**, located in Udayagiri caves near Bhubaneswar, provides detailed information about Kharavela's reign.
 
• Kharavela practiced and promoted Jainism, and he is credited with the construction and renovation of numerous Jain structures.
 
• Under his rule, Kalinga experienced significant growth in trade, commerce, and cultural exchanges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chedi Dynasty:** This dynasty was one of the ancient ruling clans mentioned in Indian history, primarily associated with the Kalinga region.
 
• **Hathigumpha Inscription:** A significant historical record engraved on a rock in Udayagiri, detailing Kharavela's achievements, military campaigns, and patronage of Jainism.
 
• **Jainism's Influence:** Kharavela was a staunch supporter of Jainism and worked towards reviving Jain traditions and infrastructure during his reign.
 
• **Kalinga's Prosperity:** During Kharavela's rule, Kalinga became a hub for trade and cultural activities, connecting it with other regions in India and beyond.
 
• **Architectural Legacy:** Kharavela is credited with initiating the construction and renovation of caves and structures, many of which are linked to the Jain religion and continue to be important archaeological sites today.
